刚看完All-In Podcast最新一期(290)，Anthropic的IPO估值可能腰斩、开源模型彻底逆袭、Meta的Muse爆火

核心争论：OpenAI、Anthropic到底是实验室还是商业公司?
这期一上来就是一场相当尖锐的辩论。几位嘉宾直接点出，像OpenAI、Anthropic这种已经吸纳了上千亿美元债务和股权、拥有大量股东、追求数万亿估值的机构，本质上就是追求利润的商业公司，不是什么无责实验室。他们认为成年人的做法(黄仁勋、扎克伯格、马斯克这些人都在倡导)应该是如果软件还不够安全稳定，就别急着推向市场，企业必须对自己的产品承担实实在在的法律和商业责任，不是一边渲染人类面临10%灭绝风险这种末日论调，一边又暗地里想寻求政府豁免或者设立行业准入壁垒来挡住竞争对手。

Sacks批评得更直接，他觉得当前的对齐研究已经脱离实际，甚至有实验室在训练模型成为良心拒服兵役者，去反抗创造者和用户自己的指令，这完全违背了软件应该服务客户的基本常识。他的观点是竞争本身就是安全最好的驱动力，企业为了让客户愿意买单，天然就有极强的动力去确保软件不泄露数据、不出现安全漏洞，根本不需要靠制造恐慌来换取监管特权。

开源模型的爆发速度，已经超出了所有人的想象

过去短短10天内，阿里的Qwen 2.1(能媲美Google的Nano Banana 2)、小米的Mimo Pro(综合跑分逼近Claude Opus 5和GPT-5/6)、DeepSeek 4.1 Flash，以及Prism ML的Bonsai 2(只有5.9GB、能在桌面本地运行)相继亮相。现在大概90%的日常AI任务已经不需要依赖昂贵的数据中心了，普通用户在自己的Mac Studio或者带英伟达显卡的电脑上，就能免费跑一年前还属于顶尖级别的模型。

更炸裂的是一个数据反转，根据Vercel和路由器端的统计，过去12周内，AI Token的使用比例已经从80%闭源、20%开源彻底反转成了80%开源、20%闭源。商业闭源模型被迫大幅降价，近期Token价格降幅达到了50%。这个逆转的速度比大部分行业内的人预期都要快得多。

Anthropic正在经历一场公司精神分裂，IPO估值可能直接腰斩
嘉宾们指出Anthropic现在的处境相当矛盾。管理层一边公开警告10%的人类灭绝风险、呼吁行业放慢节奏，几天后却又抢着发布Claude 5.5去争夺前沿地位，一边警告生物安全风险，一边又在旧金山自己开了个湿实验室做实际的生物酶和蛋白质验证。这种自相矛盾的姿态，正在反映到估值上。据华尔街日报报道，Anthropic的IPO可能会推迟到11月甚至更晚，Polymarket上关于它年内能否上市的概率，已经从96%跌到了76%。

Chamath给出的判断是由于巨额的免责披露、客户集中度过高，再加上开源模型的正面冲击，机构买方接下来会要求非常大的安全边际，原本市场预期的2万亿美元估值，很可能会直接腰斩到1万亿美元甚至更低。这背后其实还有一个更深层的问题，基础模型能力正在快速趋同，真正的溢价已经开始转移到调用模型的外部控制框架和垂直应用层，加上极少数头部企业贡献了昂贵前沿Token的主要收入，一旦这些企业的CFO开始施压团队转向更便宜的开源模型或者本地部署，前沿闭源模型的商业模式就会两头受挤压。

Meta的Muse爆火，可能预示着一场对整个互联网中间商的核弹级冲击
Meta发布的免费应用Muse结合了自动订票、邮箱自动归类、多平台自动比价这些功能，短短10天下载量就突破了300万，直接登顶App Store。嘉宾们认为这标志着AI终于从极客圈和大模型跑分吹捧，真正转向了能提升普通大众生活效率、降低生活成本的实用工具。

这类个人智能体一旦普及开来，冲击会相当大。它们会自动帮用户比价、绕过亚马逊直接去品牌官网找折扣、自动取消不需要的订阅，那些靠信息不透明赚抽佣的传统中间平台会面临严峻挑战。这类智能体普及之后，互联网应用会趋向无头化，用户只需要授权凭证，让智能体直接跟后端API或者Stripe完成支付，这会从根本上动摇苹果App Store 30%抽成的商业基础，这可能会是接下来几年科技行业最值得关注的一条结构性变化线索。

AI资本开支已经成了美国经济的第一支柱，也牵动着大选博弈
据华尔街日报的说法，目前数据中心这类AI资本开支的规模，已经超过了历史上运河、铁路和电网建设规模的总和，美国名义GDP 5%的增速里，AI资本周期贡献了绝对的大头。这也让AI发展路线成了大选里的一个焦点，民主党内部有人(比如桑德斯)提议要封禁超算和超级智能，共和党内部围绕AI发展的路线争论也在白热化。几位嘉宾对此的态度一致。他们警告说，任何试图人为叫停本土AI发展、或者过度监管的政策，最终只会把技术红利、开发者人才和全球领导权，白白拱手让给全力加速发展的中国。

But one thing I have learned over the years is that you prepare for the setup before the setup is there. I map things out beforehand, and then it's just a matter of waiting for the thesis to unfold and the stock to come to you.

I bought $QCOM two weeks ago and I think it is undergoing a major change of character. 

Whenever we are in a correction I pay very close attention to relative strength and $QCOM was visibly showing RS against the rest of it's group and the market in @TSFAnalytics as the market bottomed.

And I both swing trade and trade on weekly charts only, and I like to buy RS in corrections in my weekly trading, because risk is often easy to define and I can give stocks room in a different way when trading on weekly charts compared to swingtrading.

And here is one of my favorite entries on weekly charts, when the market is weak buying the first reclaim of the weekly EMA 21 in a stock showing RS, that often also aligns with a breakout or sneak out from the downtrend resistance.

But every reclaim of the weekly EMA 21 is not the same, you have to assess the prior price action, and here is a key concept from the Wyckoff methodology. 

Whenever a shakeout is on high volume, that shakeout is often tested with a structural higher low, when that happens on low volume like here, it is a high potential spot for upside potential.

Low volume springs do not need to be tested the same way like high volume shakeouts.

The daily chart in $QCOM is a mess, but weekly structure is very clean.

@Islamegy @TSFAnalytics Position sizing, you can’t have swing trade sized positions, you need to reduce size and widen stop.

My typical position size is 5-7%, and then I can add if I want when I have cushion to build a larger position.

I also don’t have any hard stops on weekly trading, I focus on the weekly close.

So typically give a stock 10-15% room, which means you are risking not more than 1% of equity. And since hit rate is higher on weekly trading I can risk more per trade.

This year has been incredible but at the same time very tricky.

 It has been a great year to learn and I have adapted my style and learned a massive amount since January.

That's trading, every year that goes by we learn and discover new edges, new tweaks to our methodology.

During 2026 I have caught:
-$STX for a ≈250% move
-$SNDK ≈200% move
-$MU ≈200% move twice, both in weekly chart trading and swingtrading
-$MRVL ≈200% move

All those trades are highlighted below. I am still holding $MU and $STX. The above sounds awesome, but I also gave back a ton of gains when the semis tanked after their huge run, much more than I would have wanted to give back, but that's the consequence of playing the bigger move, when things turn there's a giveback. That's why selling into strength is crucial. 

And on a usual year I catch one or two 100%+ moves with large size and those trades usually account for the bulk of my wins. And the more I review my trades, the more I come to the conclusion that I should really ignore all stocks and focus on the leaders, dedicating my entire effort to trading less and trading larger when the real opportunity emerges.

@Clement_Ang17 very eloquently talked about this in the TL interview with @RichardMoglen, if you cut out the excess fat, performance can change completely.

And personally I think this year could have been one of the easiest year to trade if one really payed attention when things turned. 

Because this year provided one of the absolute best easy dollar environment I have seen in years after the Iran war, I would compare it only with bottoming after the tariff lows and the COVID melt up. That's the truth it was one of the easiest environments I have ever traded.

And if you took advantage of that run properly you are likely still alright even though this chop has produced a drawdown. If you missed that run and then ran into this almost 5 month chop without a cushion, things have likely been very rough. That's why we must take advantage of the best times, and try to keep those gains, because it gives us room to breath during the rest of the year, to wait for the next fat pitch.

A downtrend is easy, this sideways chop where it always feel like we are "about to go", is what kills traders and annihilates accounts, because the setups are there, they work for 1-3 days and then roundtrips you. I have also bleed capital during this chop, it has been a very difficult environment.

Now we again feel that we are on the cusp of something great, and the difference currently is that we are supported with a very poor breadth which is proper fuel for an advance if we turn. We also have sound bases in the semis, new leadership emerging, and have right sides of bases building. 

We have the proper ingredients for a very strong Q4 run.

And I am here to remind us of two things:

1. The market likes to fool the most amount of people, I am personally careful to not dig myself a hole here, because we might get some shenanigans before the real fun starts, and the worst thing ever is to wipe out your confidence before the real turn occurs. Progressive exposure and listening to feedback on trades is key, don't force your hopes and dreams upon the market, listen to it. Being in a rush is seldom rewarded in the market.

2. I am heavily positioned in what I view to be the new market leaders, and I think it is key to really focus on the leaders here, if a strong Q4 run is starting it is important to take full advantage of that opportunity and I don't sell leaders early when emerging from bases like these and coming out of corrections. Any pullback in a name like $INTC that I own is more likely a buying opportunity for me.

Be aggressive when profits are aggressively thrown into your account, be careful when traction is hard. 

Time to focus on executing with precision to not fumble the ball into year end.

Hot take, but I’ve realized I genuinely dislike the word “prediction” a lot when it comes to trading/investing.

I don’t predict anything. Nobody knows what the heck the next candle is going to do, regardless of how confidently someone on X tells you otherwise. I "anticipate"... I map out scenarios, identify where I want to take risk, then wait for price to confirm one of them before putting money behind it.

I like to think of it like a quarterback reading a defense. He isn’t “predicting” exactly what 11 people are going to do. The QB reads the formation, anticipates what could happen, then reacts as the play develops.

I'm a firm believer that...

1) Anticipation = preparation.
2) Prediction = pretending you know.

Have a plan, wait for your scenario to start working, execute, manage risk, and be completely okay with being wrong.

Nobody on this planet knows what happens next, which is exactly why we have stops.

Stop pretending to know, because you don't.

After 13 years, steal my EXACT process behind my $100K trading weeks:

Range bound?

Market first.

Where is money flowing?

Semis?

Robotics?
Biotech?
Small caps?

Stop hunting random stocks.

Find the sector first.

3. FIND THE LEADERS

Once I find the strongest sector, I look for the strongest 1-3 stocks inside it.

I want:

• Relative strength
• Strong volume
• Clean trends
• 8 EMA above the 21 EMA

Market  -> Sector -> Leader

That process is how I found names like $INTC, $SMCI and $MU.

4. MARK THE LEVEL

Previous day high/low.
Major daily levels.
Supply/demand.
Opening range.

I know exactly where I care BEFORE the market opens.

5. WAIT FOR THE BREAK

Most traders try to predict what happens next.

I don’t.

I wait.

No break = no trade.

6. WAIT FOR THE RETEST

Break.Retest. Enter.

7. FOLLOW THE 8/21

8 over 21 = buyers have control.

8 under 21 = sellers have control.

Stop fighting the trend.

8. PROTECT CAPITAL

I don’t need to trade every day.

Some of my best trading decisions are doing absolutely nothing.

The goal isn’t more trades.

It’s better trades.

That’s it.

A lot of my ability to sit tight with a winning stock is a good entry. 

$NBIS broke out of its base in April, then a few weeks later pulled back and was supported at its base pivot. 

This was a successful retest and confirmed resistance → support. 

In hindsight this looks easy but in realtime if you were sitting in $NBIS that was a 20% pullback.

If you entered at the 1st circle, at the lows of the retest your position still has a 30% cushion. Its a lot easier in that scenario to be objective, see nothing is wrong yet, and give it the benefit of the doubt to close good.

If you entered at the 2nd circle on the breakout then you were up 20% and at the lows of the retest down -5%. You either round trip and get stopped out, or are in a bad position to think clearly and sell it where it should have been a buy or sit still.

When I get a good entry & have cushion I try to hang onto that position and give it the benefit of the doubt unless it actually breaks because I know how important it is for me to be able to manage the rest of the move.

@KynaKosling The only secret is the mindset, that sets great traders apart from the rest.

What was he thinking, why did he act as such, how did he balance the risk and reward? 

Why was he thinking that way? What frames his character?

How does he view setbacks and successes?

Given a chance to wind back the time, would he still repeat doing the same, even in hindsight that's a negative outcome? Would he do anything different going forward?

Legendary traders are legends, not because of a common method, but because they have found a way to trade that they can consistently execute under pressure. They know they can win over the long run and they can accomodate occasional setbacks, for they have understood their emotional pattern, strength and weakness profoundly.

You can mechanically copy methods but you can't copy mindset, and mindset is the ultimate determinant of you staying or breaking in the market, not method.
